02 / REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE / DISTRIBUTED COGNITIVE ARCHITECTURE

The architecture of persistent autonomy.

DCA is Asentxia’s reference architecture for persistent, governed autonomous intelligence. It separates a durable principal from the replaceable cognition, processes, credentials, runtimes, and hosts that may serve it.

SEVEN RESPONSIBILITIES

Seven responsibilities

A principal does not become durable because a model has memory. DCA defines seven mandatory responsibilities around identity, action, continuity, and accountability.

  • 01 · EnvironmentBounded operating environment and lifecycle
  • 02 · StateOwned, attributable, recoverable durable state
  • 03 · AuthorityExplicit, scoped, attenuable and revocable capability
  • 04 · ExecutionContained, mediated action
  • 05 · EvidenceInspectible intent, decisions, transition and outcome
  • 06 · CoordinationSeparation among identifiable principals
  • 07 · Cognition BoundaryExplicit interfaces to replaceable cognition

THE EFFECT BOUNDARY

The Effect Boundary

Proposed action crosses into consequential effect only after current authority, policy, execution context, failure state, and evidence requirements converge. The Effect Boundary is cross-cutting; it is not an eighth responsibility.

Cognition may propose. It does not authorize itself.

THE ENDURING INVARIANT

The enduring invariant

A VERA is a persistent autonomous principal, distinct from its current model, session, process, credential, runtime, or host. Topology changes do not silently expand authority. Durable state retains ownership and lineage. Evidence remains independent of self-report.

The principal persists. The components may change.

FROM ARCHITECTURE TO IMPLEMENTATION

From architecture to implementation

DCA defines the architecture. Continuum is the flagship reference implementation. The current verified slice is a bounded same-host process-restart demonstration; full DCA conformance remains a separate evidence obligation.
